low: The room has already made up its mind about you. Prove it wrong, or do not.
They reviewed your file and were not impressed. The board will decide what they could not.
No one here asked for you, Commander. Every square you take will have to argue otherwise.
mid: They will follow. For now. The board is set.
Your appointment surprised no one and convinced no one. Command anyway.
The roster is watching, undecided. First orders weigh more than first impressions.
high: They would walk into fire for you. Do not waste it.
Your reputation arrived before you did — all of it good, all of it fragile.
They already believe, Commander. Belief like that is a debt; spend it well.

low: They have heard how the last command went. The second King asks harder questions.
Word travels faster than orders. This room knows exactly what you cost.
A new King, an old reputation. They will not be fooled twice.
mid: The second appointment begins. They have heard stories; they are waiting to see which are true.
Another King, another roster's worth of doubt. The record walks in ahead of you.
They know your name here. Whether that helps is up to the next match.
high: The last command's survivors speak well of you. This room expects the same.
They asked for you by name — the second King honors what you built.
Your reputation carried across courts. Do not let it carry you past the work.

low: The last King will sit for you — once. This room has read everything.
Third appointment, final patience. They agreed to see whether the stories were unfair.
No more Kings after this one, Commander. The room knows that as well as you do.
mid: The final appointment. They will follow a while longer — the alternative is worse.
One King left willing to start a match with you. Everything now is evidence.
The third and last room. They are tired of commanders; be something else.
high: Even the last King has heard you are worth the risk. Do not make a liar of the record.
The final command, and still they hope. That hope is the rarest thing you own.
They saved the most patient King for last, because they wanted to believe in you.
